title: I made "AI Game Developer" for Unity
author: BAIZOR
selftext:
# ✨ AI Game Developer — Unity MCP (Model Context Protocol for Unity)

![AI Game Developer banner](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP/raw/main/docs/img/promo/ai-developer-banner.jpg)

I built **AI Game Developer (Unity MCP)** — an AI-powered assistant for **Unity Editor _and_ Runtime** that connects LLM clients like **Claude, Cursor, and Windsurf** to Unity via **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**, so you can automate workflows, generate code, debug faster, and even **use AI inside your compiled game**.

---

## Why this exists

Most “AI for Unity” tools stop at editor-time suggestions. This project goes further:

- It works **in the Editor** (automation, scene setup, asset work, debugging)
- It also works **in Runtime** (inside a built game) for real-time debugging and player/AI interactions

---

## Key features

- **Runtime AI** — use LLMs directly inside your compiled game (NPC behavior, debugging, live tooling)
- **Natural conversation** — talk to Unity like you talk to a teammate
- **Code assistance + tests** — ask AI to write code and run tests
- **Debug support** — ask AI to pull logs and help fix issues
- **Multiple LLM providers** — Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Microsoft, and more
- **Flexible deployment** — local (stdio) or remote (http) by config
- **Extensible** — add your own MCP Tools directly in project code

## Built-in toolset (high level)

The plugin ships with a broad default toolset — including asset operations, GameObject/component manipulation, scenes, scripts, console logs, reflection helpers, test runners, and package management.

That means you can ask things like:

```text
Explain my scene hierarchy
Create 3 cubes in a circle with radius 2
Create metallic golden material and attach it to a sphere gameObject
```

---

## Quick start

### 1) Install the Unity plugin

- **Installer**: download and import the `.unitypackage`
- **OpenUPM**:

```bash
openupm add com.ivanmurzak.unity.mcp
```

### 2) Install an MCP client

Pick one primary client (you don’t need all of them): Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.

### 3) Configure the client (automatic)

Inside Unity:

- Open your project
- Go to `Window/AI Game Developer (Unity-MCP)`
- Click **Configure** for your MCP client

---

## Extending it: add your own MCP Tools & Prompts

One of the core ideas is: **you can expose your own gameplay/editor functionality as tools**, so the AI can call them when appropriate.

Example pattern (attributes + tool method):

```csharp
[McpPluginToolType]
public class Tool_GameObject
{
    [McpPluginTool("MyCustomTask", Title = "Create a new GameObject")]
    public string CustomTask(string inputData)
    {
        return MainThread.Instance.Run(() =>
        {
            return $"[Success] Operation completed.";
        });
    }
}
```

You can also inject reusable, role-based prompts via `MCP Prompt` types.

---

## Runtime usage (inside a compiled game)

If you want AI-enabled debugging or player/AI interactions in runtime, the project supports it directly:

```csharp
UnityMcpPlugin.BuildAndStart();
UnityMcpPlugin.Connect();
UnityMcpPlugin.Disconnect();
```

There’s also a sample approach demonstrating an **AI-powered chess bot** via MCP Tools.

---

## Server & deployment (Docker / stdio / HTTP)

The Unity MCP server supports Docker deployment and both transports: `streamableHttp` and `stdio`.

Example Docker run:

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 ivanmurzakdev/unity-mcp-server
```
